answer: Co-op and Career Services: phone 00961 25 603090 ext. 414, e-mail coop@rhu.edu.lb, website www.rhu.edu.lb/coop.

source_quote: The Co-op training program bridges the intense learning experience of university and
answer: The Co-op program lets students apply classroom knowledge in a real workplace, clarifying career goals, building workplace understanding, time-management and communication skills, employer contacts, and marketable skills.

source_quote: Students may arrange for a training opportunity on their own, or the Co-op and
answer: Students may arrange a training opportunity on their own, or the Co-op and Career Services Assistant helps find a venue; training opportunities are approved and managed by the Co-op Coordinator with the academic advisor.

source_quote: A student may opt to complete the Co-op training at a reputable institution abroad,
answer: A student may complete Co-op training at a reputable institution abroad subject to approvals; they must submit the Training Abroad Application Form (Co-op-12) to the Co-op and Career Services Assistant.

source_quote: Students may register for one course during the Co-op period if it is the only course
answer: Students may register for one course during the Co-op period only if it is the only course needed to graduate and the employer approves the timing in writing.

source_quote: The Co-op program runs for at least eight weeks, 8 hours per day, and is normally
answer: Co-op training lasts at least eight weeks, 8 hours per day, and is normally completed in the summer term of the third year of studies.

source_quote: The Co-op work supervisor cannot be a direct relative of the trainee;
answer: The Co-op work supervisor cannot be a direct relative of the trainee. The organization must be reputable and not owned by the student's parent, and the student may not work in a department where a family member works.

source_quote: Students can only withdraw from the Co-op course upon approval from the Co-op
answer: Students can withdraw from the Co-op course only with approval of the Co-op academic advisor and the Co-op and Career Services Assistant. Failing to comply with Co-op rules or the employer's standards results in a failing grade.

source_quote: Completing ENGL 217 and the requisite number of credits with a GPA of at least
answer: To join Co-op, a bachelor's student must complete ENGL 217 and the required credits with a GPA of at least 70, be enrolled during the training period, and complete the college pre-training requirements: senior standing, passing ENGL 217, and a CGPA of 70 or higher.
The Co-op course is 1 credit in Engineering and in Business Administration, and 1-3 credits in Arts and Sciences.

source_quote: In preparation for the Co-op training, students must attend the Co-op Policies and
answer: Before Co-op, students must attend the Co-op Policies and Procedures, CV Writing, and Interview Skills seminars.

source_quote: Information for Co-op requests outside the offerings of the Co-op and Career Services
answer: A student who secures their own venue must give the Co-op and Career Services Assistant, in early spring, the employer and supervisor contact information and employment conditions for approval: organization name, company profile/website, job description/training plan, supervisor name, contact person and details.

source_quote: Each eligible student completes the Co-op Application Form (Co-op-3), indicating
answer: Each eligible student submits the Co-op Application Form (Co-op-3) listing three ranked preferred venues plus a soft-copy CV by the deadline. Matching happens within two weeks; when students compete for a spot, those who applied first and meet eligibility get priority. Employers may interview students before the assignment.

source_quote: The student should read, understand, and complete the Co-op Code of Conduct
answer: The Co-op office creates a Co-op Moodle course for eligible students, posts opportunities and assignments there and by email, and holds an orientation seminar in early spring. Students must complete the Co-op Code of Conduct before the Co-op begins.

source_quote: The academic advisor bears the responsibility to make at least one field visit and
answer: Each trainee has a Co-op academic advisor who makes at least one field visit, follows up with the trainee and supervisor, collects assessment forms, guides the report, poster and presentation, and submits a final report.

source_quote: submit in the last week of the Co-op period the following:
answer: Trainees must submit the Trainee's Assessment of Training Form, a training tasks log, a formal report, a poster, and a PowerPoint presentation, participate in the Co-op poster exhibition, and present at the Co-op Inspiration Seminar when requested.

answer: Co-op is graded Pass with Honors (PH), Pass (P), or Fail (F) based on employer evaluation, advisor assessment, report, log, poster, and presentation. PH requires outstanding evaluations; an F requires repeating the whole Co-op experience.

Career Services builds an employer database, announces job vacancies to students and alumni, runs CV and interview seminars, keeps a CV data bank and sends CVs to employers, and organizes an annual job fair.

answer: Job vacancies (often with the company name kept confidential) are posted on the official RHU Alumni LinkedIn page; alumni apply by sending an updated CV to Coop@rhu.edu.lb, and the office forwards CVs to employers and follows up.
